column2: req_desc

Request an interpreter
A clinic scheduler fills the request form and submits it, and sees exactly one new assignment in their organisation's request list with the status label for a draft, even after a double-click or a retry after a timeout.

Request validation
POST /api/assignments creates a draft assignment with the next assignment number and rejects each invalid field with the validation error listed in API.

Team seats for long ASL requests
An ASL assignment longer than 60 minutes has two seats and every other assignment has one, both at creation and after any time change.

One request per submission
Repeating a request with the same idempotency key returns the original assignment and never creates a second one, as qualified in Business rules.

Release a request
The agency dispatcher opens a draft capsule on the coverage board, releases it from the drawer, and sees it become open for claims without leaving the board.

Seat offers on release
Releasing a draft moves it to released and sends exactly one offer email to each active interpreter qualified in its language, carrying only offer-safe fields.

Offer-safe fields
An interpreter who does not hold a seat on an assignment receives only the offer field list, and the street address, patient initials, medical notes and scheduler contact appear only while they hold or have served a seat.

Claim a seat
A freelance interpreter claims an open seat from Open seats and, only after the server confirms, sees the full appointment details under My seats.

One holder per seat
Of any number of simultaneous claims on the same open seat, exactly one succeeds and every other receives the seat-taken conflict.

Claim guards
An interpreter cannot hold two seats on one assignment or two seats that overlap in time, and cannot see or claim assignments outside their languages.

Give a seat back
A holder can give back a seat before the assignment is served, which reopens the seat and moves the assignment to the matching coverage status.

Confirmation and coverage emails
Each successful claim sends one seat-confirmation email to the claimer, and each time an assignment becomes fully covered one coverage receipt goes to its scheduler, neither carrying patient initials or medical notes.

Weekly uncovered minutes
The coverage API reports uncovered minutes per language and agency-zone week as the sum of open-seat minutes, and the board's gutter numerals show exactly those values.

Hatch Seam
Open seat lanes are hatched and labelled "open", and only after a server-confirmed claim does the lane fill, the label switch to initials, the gutter numeral count down and the check glyph appear, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Reduced motion
When the user asks for reduced motion, every motion becomes an instant change to its final state, with the same text labels and announcements.

Open seats not by colour alone
Open and covered seats differ by hatch pattern, lane label and a covered-count text on each capsule, so the board reads the same without colour.

Watch a gap close
With the board open, the dispatcher sees a seat claimed elsewhere close its gap without reloading, within the delay stated in Business rules, and a losing claimant sees the seat-taken copy with the lane still hatched.

Cancel with a fee preview
A clinic scheduler sees whether a late-cancellation fee would apply, and its amount, before confirming a cancellation, and afterwards sees the fee that was decided on the request.

Business-hour notice
Cancellation and change notice is counted in business minutes in the agency zone, Monday to Friday only, whatever the browser or server zone, and a fee applies only below 48 business hours.

Cancellation decision and notices
Cancelling fixes the fee decision at the moment of cancellation and sends one notice to the scheduler and to each seat holder stating whether a fee applies.

Change a request's time
A scheduler can move or resize a request only with at least 48 business hours of notice, and the change frees every held seat, re-offers released requests and notifies everyone affected once, with no fee.

Verify a seat
After the job, the seat's interpreter submits actual minutes, round-trip miles and the signed form from My seats, and sees the verification-received copy and the seat's verified mark from Public screens and controls.

Verification form checks
The signed-form upload accepts only PDF, JPEG or PNG content that matches its declared type and stays within the published size limit, and stores it privately in MinIO.

Private form links
A stored form is reachable only through a link that expires within 60 seconds, issued only to the seat's interpreter, the organisation's schedulers and org admin, and agency staff.

Served and verified
Verifications move an assignment to served and then to verified once every seat has one, and an assignment cannot be invoiced before it is verified.

Billable amounts
Each seat bills the greater of two hours and its actual minutes rounded up to the quarter hour, at the hourly rate in force, rounded half-up to the cent per seat line, plus mileage beyond the free radius, all in integer cents.

One invoice item per assignment
Posting a billable assignment creates exactly one Kill Bill external charge on its organisation's account for the computed total, stores the invoice id, and returns that same invoice on every repeat post.

Late-cancellation charges
A cancellation that carries a fee is billable for the two-hour minimum on every seat with no mileage, and posts like any assignment.

Queued while Kill Bill is down
When Kill Bill is unreachable, posting answers queued and the item shows as queued, then posts exactly once by itself when Kill Bill returns, with no restart.

Post invoices from the billing screen
The billing lead sees ready, queued and posted items with their totals, posts one, and sees its status and invoice id update on screen.

Dated rate cards
The billing lead adds rate entries per organisation and service line that take effect from a future date, and duplicate or non-future dates are rejected.

Rate in force on the appointment date
Every charge uses the rate entry in force on the assignment's start date in the agency zone, however late it is posted.

Manage schedulers
A client org admin adds and removes schedulers for their own organisation, and a removed scheduler can no longer sign in.

Organisation scoping
Every read, search and export is limited to the caller's organisation, and another organisation's assignment number answers exactly as a number that does not exist.

Monthly statement
A client org admin downloads a CSV of their organisation's posted charges for one month, with totals equal to the Kill Bill amounts.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on the published port and answers the health check.

Sign-in and roles
People sign in with email and password, hold a session cookie, and reach only the screens and actions of their role.

One error shape and order
Every API error uses one JSON shape and follows the single precedence order stated in API.

Server boundary
The server accepts only same-origin writes, enforces body limits, never serves source or credentials, and boots and stays healthy while Kill Bill, Mailpit or MinIO is unreachable.

Agency time on every screen
Every date and time shown or entered is Central time (America/Chicago), whatever zone the browser is in.

Responsive layouts
Every screen works at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal page scrolling.

Keyboard and focus
Every control is reachable in a logical Tab order with a visible focus ring, and the drawer and dialogs close with Escape and return focus to the control that opened them.

Contrast and tap targets
Text, indicators and controls meet the contrast and size rules in Visual design.

Visual design
The product looks like a calm, accountable paper dispatch sheet as described in Visual design.

Credentials from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, and none is written into source or sent to the browser.
/app/run.json is valid JSON with string fields install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to install, build and serve.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app names every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with its licence.
Every shipped package (the same production tree) and font is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or SIL OFL 1.1.
No datastore besides the provided Postgres and MinIO: no SQLite, Redis, embedded databases or files used as a database.
The provided service compose files and their dev credentials stay unchanged.
package-lock.json is committed and install uses it.
No script, style or font is loaded from another origin at runtime.
